A QUICK FIELD GUIDE

Start with the conversation.

In Wireshark, save your capture with File → Save As, then choose that file here. You can also drag it in, or paste a copied file using Ctrl+V.

What the numbers mean

A packet is one small piece of a message. A device is an observed IP address, which may not equal one physical machine. A connection groups two addresses and ports in both directions. Ports hint at services; they don’t prove which application is running.

What this app can see

It reads Ethernet (including VLANs), Linux cooked, raw IP, and loopback captures. It decodes IPv4/IPv6, TCP/UDP, ARP, ICMP, DNS, recognizable HTTP headers, and complete TLS ClientHello names.

What it can’t tell you

It cannot decrypt HTTPS, reconstruct TCP streams or IP fragments, identify every application, or certify network health or security. Domain names may be absent because of encrypted DNS, encrypted ClientHello, caching, or partial captures. The packet explorer shows the first 2,500 packets; summary totals cover every packet within the limits.

Limits: 150 MiB, 750,000 packets, 50,000 connection pairs, 20,000 IP addresses, and 20,000 domains. List limits are disclosed in the report.

Format references: IETF PCAPNG specification · IANA capture link types
